BMS Threat Guide - Air Defense Vehicle charts (AN/ALR-69(V)/ALR-56M and AN/ALR-93(V)1), radar and aircraft entries
BMS Training Manual 4.38.1 - ramp start (TWA/TWP), Missions 12 and 28
overview: The RWR detects and identifies radar emissions painting the aircraft and shows each emitter as an alphanumeric symbol on the azimuth indicator (scope) at its bearing. BMS models the different RWRs fitted to the F-16 variants - AN/ALR-56M (USAF F-16CM), AN/ALR-69(V) (older/European F-16s), AN/ALR-93(V)1 (e.g. F-16C Blk 52+ and F-CK-1), plus Thales CARAPACE, ALR-67(V)3 (F/A-18) and Elisra SPS-1000/3000 - each with its own display, sounds, controls, library and direction-finding accuracy (15 deg in E-J band, omnidirectional in C/D band for ALR-56M/69/93). Distance of a symbol from the scope center is NOT proportional to real range (ambiguities are modelled), and the emitter symbols differ between RWR types (the Threat Guide lists ALR-69/ALR-56M symbols on top and ALR-93 symbols below). Priority: the RWR ranks emitters by lethality (SAM dat files give LOW and HIGH altitude lethality scores - ALTITUDE button selects the bias); PRIORITY mode shows only the 5 most lethal tracks, OPEN mode up to 12 (16 with UNKNOWN on). The diamond (HANDOFF modes) marks the highest priority or selected emitter and its audio is played continuously. Fire control radars in track are boxed, a flashing circle around a symbol together with the red flashing LAUNCH light and the missile launch tone indicates a radar-guided missile being guided on ownship. Search radars are only shown when SEARCH is selected (S flashes when filtered search radars are painting you) and unknown emitters only when UNKNOWN is selected (U flashes). New emitters trigger the "new guy" alert (3 bursts of sound in 1.5 s, symbol pulsing to 1.5x size for 4 s). Listen for the tone change from SA (search/acquisition) to FC (fire control): most SAMs fire shortly after it. Some systems give no launch warning at all (SA-10, SA-20, Patriot) and IR SAMs/optical AAA never appear on the RWR. Before taxi: power the system at the Threat Warning Aux panel (SYSTEM POWER), run SYS TEST and LAUNCH light/audio test at the Threat Warning Prime, then press HANDOFF once to enter diamond float mode - omitting this leaves the RWR in normal (quiet) mode.

symbols.details: Unknown-type radars are shown only when UNKNOWN mode is selected (display shows up to 16 symbols). When UNKNOWN is off but unknown radars paint ownship, the U on the UNKNOWN button flashes at 4 Hz. On the ALR-93, unknown/AAA/search/CW emitters get a 2-character numeric code (see alr93SymbolCodes).

With SEARCH mode on, emitters detected in an air search radar mode are shown as S symbols (and S in the scope center on ALR-56M/69). With SEARCH off, the S on the button flashes at 4 Hz when search radars paint ownship. ALR-93: search radars are only in the training library (LIB SET).

Shown in diamond float (floats to the highest priority symbol), transient (steps down the priority list while HANDOFF is held) and latch (stays on the last selected symbol) modes; the audio of that emitter is heard continuously. Inhibited in normal mode. The same threat is repeated on the HMCS (diamond on the circle at its bearing, ID in the center) when RWR DSPLY is ON.

The RWR flashes a circle about the threat on its scope, the red MISSILE LAUNCH light on the Threat Warning Prime flashes (4 Hz) and the missile launch tone sounds when a radar missile is being guided on ownship. The RWR will not step to it automatically if the diamond is latched on another threat.

symbols.meaning: Signal correlated with a target tracking radar
symbols.details: A box is drawn around the symbol when the emitter signal is correlated with a target tracking radar.
A new emitter alternates between normal size and 1.5 times normal size for its first 4 seconds of display, with 3 bursts of its sound in 1.5 s.
ALR-93: octagon + a beep every 7 seconds = lock (STT). No beep = track (SAM/TWS or similar).
Displayed after single-character emitters in track mode. Because of the 2-character limit it cannot be added to 2-character symbols - use the octagon/beep cue instead.
KS-12, KS-19 and S-60 guns directed by the Fire Can radar show alternating A and S flashing. ALR-93 shows K.
Alternating 15 and M flashing on the RWR.
ALTITUDE button selects the low altitude threat table (ALR-56M/69).
After boot "I" is shown in the middle of the scope, then "WO"; indications disappear when the initial BIT finishes.

After self-test, a detected fault shows the fault list (ALR-56M) or flashing BAD on the second test screen (ALR-69), then the normal display with F in the middle. ALR-69 also shows F briefly during boot.
Toggled by pressing SYS TEST and then UNKNOWN within 0.5-1 s. ALR-56M has no SEA mode - naval emitters are always visible.
symbols.source: BMS Technical Manual (Threat Warning Prime callbacks); TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 2.7.3.3.1

symbols.meaning: Band noise (graphical only) and signal load
symbols.details: Four noise bars at 6, 9, 12 and 3 o'clock (bands 0-3) are graphical only. The cycle timer (vertical bar at the left end of the band 3 bar) moves up and down in 1 s with no signal activity and slows to 2.6 s with full RWR activity.

STBY = ECM off, A = ECM AVNC (XMT 2, auto ECM priority), E = ECM ECM (XMT 3, active jam). ALR-93 also shows CMDS mode and ECM state at the top, ECM interference indications at the bottom and ECM unavailable at the right.

symbols.meaning: Threat bearing repeated in the HUD
symbols.details: Threat at 12 o'clock at the top of the HUD, 3 o'clock on the right, etc. Longer line = threat in the inner RWR circle, shorter line = outer circle, flashing line = missile launch detected.

Symbol distance from center is not proportional to actual distance. The Threat Guide notes e.g. the SA-10 Big Bird "10 has lower sound and stays in outer ring" while the Flap Lid has a "higher chirp inner ring".
symbols.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 2.7.3 (intro); BMS Threat Guide (Big Bird, Flap Lid B)

symbols.details: Standard RWR convention for air threats; the BMS docs only show it in figures.

tones.name: New guy alert
tones.description: In normal mode threat audio is limited to the new guy alert and launch audio: 3 bursts of the new emitter's sound in 1.5 seconds.

tones.name: Priority / handoff emitter audio
tones.description: In diamond float, transient and latch modes the sound of the diamond-enhanced emitter is heard continuously (composite audio); each emitter type has its own sound.

tones.name: Search (SA) to fire control (FC) tone change
tones.description: RWR sounds are subtle: listen for the tone change from SA to FC - most SAMs will shoot shortly after it. Examples: Hawk FC tone at 19 NM on the first run in (33 NM second time); Patriot has no launch warning - assume a launch if you hear the FC tone.
tones.source: BMS Threat Guide (General notes, AN/MPQ-46, AN/MPQ-53)

tones.name: Chirp / pitch by ring
tones.description: Threat Guide notes: SA-10 Flap Lid "higher chirp inner ring"; the Big Bird 5N64S "10 has lower sound and stays in outer ring".
tones.source: BMS Threat Guide (Flap Lid B, Big Bird)

tones.name: Missile launch tone
tones.description: TWS missile launch tone in the headset when a radar missile is being guided on ownship, with the flashing circle on the scope and flashing red LAUNCH light. It is a fixed-volume warning tone.

tones.name: TWS composite tone volume
tones.description: THREAT knob on AUDIO 1 panel: clockwise increases the TWS composite tone volume (can be mapped to an analog axis). The launch tone is not affected (fixed volume).

tones.name: ALR-93 lock beep
tones.description: Octagon plus a beep every 7 seconds = STT lock; no beep = track (SAM/TWS).

tones.name: CARAPACE voice
tones.description: After power-up a female voice informs of any faults (FAIL light; clears only by power cycle).

controls.name: HANDOFF (ALR-56M/69, diamond "H" lamp)
controls.description: Short push (<1 s): toggles normal <-> diamond float mode. Press and hold (>1 s): transient mode, diamond steps down the priority list; release = latch on the last symbol (returns to float if that emitter times out). Lamp on when a handoff mode is engaged. Mouse: left-click = short push, right-click = long push (click again to release). Recommended: diamond float for maximum SA.

controls.name: MODE (PRI / OPEN)
controls.description: Toggles PRIORITY (only the 5 most lethal tracks) and OPEN (up to 12 tracks, 16 with UNKNOWN). PRI lamp flashes at 4 Hz in PRIORITY mode when more than 5 radars are painting ownship.

controls.name: LAUNCH (MISSILE LAUNCH)
controls.description: Red, flashes at 4 Hz when a radar missile is being guided on ownship. Pressing tests the launch light (and audio during the preflight BIT).
controls.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 2.7.3.1.4, 2.7.3.2.1; Training Manual ramp start

controls.name: SYS TEST
controls.description: Initiates self-test (two test screens, then fault list/F if faulty). Can be used to reset the RWR if it gets stuck. ALR-69: SYS TEST then UNKNOWN within 0.5 s toggles naval (SEA) mode.

controls.name: T / TGT SEP
controls.description: Spreads out overlapping emitter symbols for 5 seconds, then the display returns to normal.

controls.name: UNKNOWN (U)
controls.description: Toggles UNKNOWN mode (shows up to 16 symbols including unknown-type emitters). U flashes when unknown radars are painting but filtered.

controls.name: SEARCH (S)
controls.description: Toggles SEARCH mode (S symbols for emitters in air search mode). S flashes when search radars paint ownship while filtered.

controls.name: ACT/PWR (ACTIVITY / POWER)
controls.description: ACTIVITY on when missile activity (guide or tracking modes) is detected; POWER on whenever the RWR is powered. No button function.

controls.name: ALTITUDE (LOW / ALT)
controls.description: Toggles LOW and HIGH altitude threat assessment biasing (SAM dat files hold LOW and HIGH lethality scores). L shown in scope center when LOW is selected.

controls.name: SYSTEM POWER
controls.description: Toggles RWR power. First step of the defensive suite power-up on the ramp (SYSTEM POWER light illuminates); RWR and jammer are also switched ON on the CMDS panel.
controls.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 2.7.3.1.4; Training Manual ramp start

controls.name: RWR DSPLY (HMCS DISPLAY DED page)
controls.description: Displays the RWR priority (diamond) threat on the HMCS. Requires a priority threat and float, transient or latch mode; in handoff OFF (normal) nothing is shown. Do not rely on it if the threat is latched.

controls.name: ALR-93: POWER / BIT / LIB SET / PRIORITY
controls.description: POWER powers the system; BIT initiates self-test (FAULT light if a fault is found); LIB SET toggles normal and training libraries (normal library does not contain search radars); PRIORITY selects priority mode.

controls.name: SPS-3000: PRI / OPN / JMR
controls.description: PRI: only the 5 highest priority threats displayed (yellow light); OPN: all threats displayed; JMR light: internal jammer ON or STBY. Otherwise same as ALR-93(V)1.

controls.name: CARAPACE: EXP / PRIO / MODE / PWR
controls.description: EXP separates overlapping contacts (double click within 1 s = self-test, BIT light); PRIO selects priority mode; MODE toggles libraries (search radars included when AI indicator on); PWR powers up. EDS AUTO / MAN ON lights show CMDS auto/manual mode.

controls.name: ALR-67(V)3: ENABLE OFFSET / ENABLE SPECIAL / LIMIT DISPLAY / POWER
controls.description: ENABLE OFFSET (Alt+Num 9, SimRWRHandoff): highest priority target for composite audio, hold to browse. ENABLE SPECIAL (Alt+Num 3, SimRWRSetTargetSep): separates overlapping contacts. LIMIT DISPLAY (Alt+Num 6, SimRWRSetPriority): priority mode. POWER (Alt+Num 0, SimRwrPower).

preflight: Threat Warning Aux: press SYSTEM POWER - SYSTEM POWER light on.
CMDS panel: RWR and JMR switches ON.
Threat Warning Prime: press SYS TEST and check the RWR display test.
Press the MSL LAUNCH indicator to test the light and audio.
Press HANDOFF once to set diamond float mode (often overlooked - without it the RWR will not warn properly).
gaps: Ship emitters: the BMS Threat Guide ship pages/charts list radars and weapons but no RWR symbols, so no ship entries are included.
Generic RWR display symbology (hat, boat, lethality rings, figures of each RWR scope) is only shown as images in the Dash-34; the "Hat" entry is flagged source "general".
Air-to-air missile pages and the aircraft/AA-missile charts (Threat Guide p.45-46) are images only; aircraft symbols were taken from the individual aircraft entries.
ALR-69 naval mode indication and ALR-93/CARAPACE symbol pages are images in the Dash-34.
Nike Hercules shows both N and P lines in the ALR-56M chart; recorded as N with a note.
